claim: The 'not already withheld by an earlier record' test is register.hit(value).ref, and Screen.hit returns the FIRST register entry with any form contained in the text, not the secret's own entry; a new CLI secret whose value contains an earlier-withheld value (or its percent or base64 form) is judged already withheld and gets no record and no stop, so Requirement 1 ('every named CLI secret ... not already withheld by an earlier record ... gets its own value-free disproof record') is unmet for that input. The predicate predates the slice (828a524 effects.py:757) but the slice's requirement now rests on it for every secret. Reverse case: a ref-less entry listed ahead of the matching ref'd one writes a duplicate record and stops on every invocation. Raised MAJOR by correctness-r2 (which notes it reads as a BLOCKER under a literal reading of the requirement), MINOR by seams-r2 and security-r2.
scenario: Register holds a disproof-read entry 'aaaa' (ref 'disproof 9'); the pull drops VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN="aaaa" and VERCEL_AUTOMATION_BYPASS_SECRET="aaaa2222"; the run description holds 'aaaa2222'. Result on head and on base: stop=False, records=0. A later status form (no pull) redacts only 'aaaa' and prints the '2222' tail.

claim: The new de-duplication (`entry not in entries`) compares register Entry objects by identity, and Screen.add keys an Entry on value plus components ([raw] is a component only when raw != value), so one secret value arriving once quoted and once raw gives two entries and two disproof records with identical rests where the base wrote one; this departs from 'a single caught secret ... works exactly as today'. No value leaks. Raised by spec-r2, correctness-r2 and seams-r2.
scenario: Dropped lines VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN="aaaa1111" and VERCEL_AUTOMATION_BYPASS_SECRET=aaaa1111 with the value in the description (or the canary test with bypass = token): head writes 2 disproof records both resting at inputs.json 37-68 (form reads '2 on record' for one value); base writes 1.

claim: The per-secret disproof records are separate journal appends in a loop, not atomic as a set; a kill after record 1 and before record 2 leaves the second secret in the run's records with no withhold record, and SEC-12's startup read (disproof.py) never re-derives CLI secrets, so the next status form writes it in clear. The resume heals it by re-pulling. The base had the same window before its single record (wider: both secrets), so this narrows rather than opens it; no kill-sweep covers the two-secret path. Raised by all four reviewers; executed by security-r2.
scenario: Canary fixture (two secrets in one pull, both in the run's description) with an in-process kill at the second pre/journal/disproof event: 1 disproof on record; the next status form status-1.txt holds the OIDC token in clear (token True, bypass False); the first resume stops and writes record 2; the second resume completes.

claim: assertNotEqual(disproofs[0]['rests'], disproofs[1]['rests']) only shows the two spans differ, not that each record reads back to a different one of the two secrets; one secret alone has several spans. The mixed case (one secret withheld by an earlier record, one new) and a kill between the appends are untested. Raised by spec-r2, correctness-r2 and security-r2.
scenario: A regression where both records rest on two different spans of the same secret (the red run shows 4 spans for one canary) passes line 48; only the later status and resume leak assertions would catch it, indirectly.

claim: The status summon's ending and the presence of a status form are never asserted, so the 'next status form withholds both' check could pass with nothing checked. Raised by spec-r2 (seams-r2 observed the same, not raised).
scenario: If a change made status produce no form (result.doc['forms'] empty), the loop over forms at the status result checks nothing and the test still passes; the reviewers' probes show a form is produced today.

claim: 'Neither holding a value' is checked only for the bare value (assertNotIn(secret, json.dumps(disproofs))), not the base64 or percent forms the register treats as the value. Raised by correctness-r2.
scenario: A disproof record that carried a base64 form of a secret would pass this assertion; low risk today since owed_for_channel holds only spans.
